subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for BrightStream - throughput model & SLO fit
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@brightstream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for BrightStream - initial calc attached

Hi Asha —

Thanks for taking the meeting this morning. Per our call, I attached a first-pass throughput model for BrightStream based on the traffic profile you shared (attached CSV). High level assumptions are in the spreadsheet; the two most important knobs are: model variant (13B vs 70B) and peak concurrency distribution.

The quick recommendation below is intended to get a conservative Dedicated sizing for the POC + first quarter of production with headroom. If we converge on these numbers I'll loop infra for a provisioning timeline.

Summary (short):
- Recommended reserved capacity: 8 x H100-80GB GPUs (reserved) with autoscale to 12 GPUs for burst.
- Model baseline: redwood-13b-q4 (prefers low-latency quantized path).
- Expected steady tokens/sec delivered: ~7,200 tokens/sec aggregate (p50); burst capacity to ~12,000 tps.
- SLO fit: p95 generation latency target 750ms for 64-token responses (with batching and prefix cache hit-rate ~25%).

Attached: redwood_throughput_estimate_v1.xlsx (details + per-GPU benchmarks)

Next steps: can you confirm the peak concurrent users and acceptable p95 latency? Also let me know if security requires Private deployment rather than Dedicated so I can update timelines.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — this looks useful. Couple clarifications from our side: 
- Peak: during business hours (10–16 PT) we see up to 600 active analysts using the feature concurrently; peak RPS spikes to ~180 with short bursts to 350 for a few minutes during reports release.
- Typical prompt size: 32 tokens; average generation requested: 160 tokens (some multi-part responses).
- SLO: product wants p95 end-to-end <= 1.2s for 160-token outputs; p50 should be < 400ms.
- Data residency: US-only for now, Dedicated is fine.

Can you update the sheet with these numbers? Also we may need to include longer context windows (2–4k) for some users — not all traffic.

— Asha
Head of Product, BrightStream
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: BrightStream sizing — engineering take (internal)

Dylan/Rishi — forwarding BrightStream's clarifications. I started a rough back-of-envelope below using their numbers; Rishi, can you validate and convert to per-GPU needs?

Back-of-envelope:
- Peak concurrent analysts: 600; assume 1 request per analyst per 20s => ~30 RPS baseline; spike to 350 RPS for bursts.
- Average tokens per request = prompt 32 + gen 160 = 192 tokens total per request.
- At 350 RPS * 192 tokens = 67,200 tokens/sec during bursts.

Per-GPU throughput assumptions (measured on our testbench, see sheet):
- H100-80GB (redwood-13b-q4): ~1,200 tokens/sec per GPU at latency envelope targeting p50~300ms, p95 depends on batching but median.
- A100-40GB: ~700 tokens/sec per GPU.

Simple capacity calc (burst):
- GPUs required = ceil(67,200 / 1,200) = 56 H100s (naive, no batching/caching).

This is obviously too big for an initial reserved pool. We should apply realistic production optimizations: batching, continuous batching, prefix caching (their usage pattern has repeated prompts), and model variants (13B for chat, 70B for high-quality but at lower traffic).

Proposal: create a two-tier routing policy:
1) Interactive chat (90% of requests): redwood-13b-q4 with aggressive batching and prefix cache — effective per-GPU throughput improves ~3.5x in steady state => ~4,200 tps.
2) High-quality analytical queries (10%): redwood-70b or ensemble on 70B quantized on A100 with lower throughput (estimate 250 tps).

Under this hybrid:
- Effective burst demand mapped to 13B path = 67,200 * 0.9 = 60,480 tps -> need ~15 H100s (60,480 / 4,200).
- High-quality path demand = 6,720 tps -> need ~27 A100s if we used A100-only (6,720 / 250 = 27), or colocate 4–6 H100s if we run 70B optimized (cost tradeoff).

I'll let Rishi run a more realistic simulator with their request histogram and caching assumptions.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightStream sizing — engineering take (internal)

Marissa — ran a small simulation with the BrightStream CSV and added fields in the attached spreadsheet (redwood_throughput_estimate_v1.xlsx). Key points: 

Assumptions used in sim:
- Traffic histogram: baseline 30 RPS 80% of time, burst to 350 RPS top 2% windows.
- Request token distribution as Asha provided; cache hit-rate for prefixes 28% (they have many repeated prompts).
- Continuous batching improves tokens/sec by 2.8x under burst (we assume sub-ms churn and we can batch across 50–75ms windows).
- We model autoscaler with 90s scale-up and 2-minute cool-down.

Results (conservative):
- Recommended reserved pool: 12 x H100 (reserved) configured for 13B optimized runtime. This handles baseline and typical bursts with p95 latency ~850ms for 160-token outputs.
- Autoscale ceiling: 40 x H100 (adds capacity in 8-GPU increments) to handle sustained heavy bursts and to keep p95 under 1.2s.
- If BrightStream must support consistent 350 RPS sustained (not short bursts), we'd recommend mixing 12 H100 (reserved) + 28 H100 burst (temporary) OR 12 H100 + 50 A100s depending on pricing.
- Cost vs headroom: 12 H100 reserved + autoscale gives ~1.5x headroom for typical weekly peaks; full sustained 350 RPS for hours will incur significant burst cost.

Action items for sales/procurement:
- Present 12 H100 reserved + autoscale to 40 policy as our recommended starting contract.
- Put explicit roundup in Deal terms: 12 reserved with option to convert up to 24 reserved at a 30-day notice.
- Draft SLA that targets p95 <= 1.2s for 160-token outputs with explicit cache/batching assumptions and a capacity runbook.

I've attached the updated workbook and a short one-page runbook snippet in the Drive link.

-Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for BrightStream - throughput model & SLO fit

Asha — we've updated the sizing after engineering validation. Short version for execs: 

Recommended commercial starting point (POC -> Q1 prod):
- 12 x H100-80GB reserved capacity for BrightStream (regional: us-west), with autoscale policy to 40 H100s for burst events.
- Recommended model routing: 90% traffic -> redwood-13b-q4 (low-latency); 10% -> 70B optimized path for analytical quality.
- Expected p95 latency under our production config: ~850ms for 160-token outputs during typical peaks; target SLA p95 <= 1.2s (to match your product ask).
- Headroom: typical weekly peaks covered with 1.5x headroom; sustained 350 RPS for >10 minutes falls into burst and will consume autoscale capacity.

We will include a clause in the contract that describes the assumptions (batch window, cache hit-rate, and model variants). If you agree, I'll start paperwork with procurement and include the runbook and SLA draft.

Also attaching SLA draft + the throughput workbook to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the numbers.
Dylan

Dylan — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detail. This looks reasonable. A few procurement notes for the contract team: 
- We prefer a 12-month reserved commitment with a trial 3-month conversion option.
- We need a clear cost model for reserved vs burst H100 pricing in the contract.
- Please add a reporting cadence for token usage and an on-call escalation contact for outages.

I'll loop Procurement next week and will share the contract template. Let's plan a 30-minute review on Wed to finalize numbers before RFP submission.
